title: FORM — Anatomy in motion
identity: One original adult blonde woman with blue eyes, shared with MUSE.
scope: Five views of one licensed skinned character: full body, arm, hand, leg and foot. The accepted SVG corpus remains separate.

studies.title: A gesture is a whole-body event.
studies.prompt: Use the shared adult female character from the licensed CC0 MakeHuman-derived GLB, with its continuous human topology, 53-bone rig, skin weights and embedded textures. Bake one fixed original identity with blonde hair, blue eyes, a softly tapered lower jaw, rounded chin, refined dentition and a neutral anatomical bodysuit; use exactly the same identity in FORM and MUSE. Keep shoulders, clavicles, waist, hips, limbs, hands and feet organically connected. Use a clean, finely textured complexion with neutral-warm facial illumination. Use the existing charcoal stage, serif interface, soft studio illumination and mint selection accent. Selected regions reuse the character surface triangles, with translucent feathered overlays and anchors that follow the evaluated skinned surface. Keep the five-second timeline, responsive controls and guided camera; manual orbit interrupts guidance. Restore the exact neutral pose at five seconds. Frame the complete character in a relaxed standing pose. Animate a controlled reach and return through the clavicle, shoulder, elbow, wrist and fingers, with a small trunk counter-turn and head response. Keep both feet supported. Preserve selectable Pectoralis region, Back and Pelvis surfaces, plus the abdominal wall, shoulder and head. Inspect front, profile, three-quarter and posterior silhouettes; do not add circular chest markings.
studies.method: Licensed CC0 MakeHuman-derived GLB topology, textures and skinning; one locally selected adult identity; authored deterministic skeletal animation; surface-triangle overlays and posed anchors. The mesh is externally authored asset data, not a new procedural sculpt or scan.

parts.name: Pectoralis region
parts.description: The pectoral region spans the upper chest beneath the bodysuit. Follow its continuous connection toward the shoulder as the arm reaches.

parts.name: Back
parts.description: The posterior trunk supports posture during the reach. This surface overlay follows the back as the torso turns. Selecting Back fades the hair so its surface stays visible; clearing the selection restores the hair.

parts.name: Pelvis
parts.description: The pelvis joins trunk and lower limbs. The highlighted surface indicates the pelvic region beneath the bodysuit.

parts.name: Abdominal wall
parts.description: The abdominal surface links the ribcage to the pelvis and moves with the trunk.

parts.name: Deltoid region
parts.description: The shoulder contour blends continuously into the upper arm. The skin follows the imported shoulder rig.

parts.name: Head & gaze
parts.description: The same adult character appears in FORM and MUSE. The head turns gently toward the reaching hand.

beats.label: Prepare
beats.description: The connected character establishes the resting pose before the movement begins.

beats.label: Reach
beats.description: The shoulder lifts the arm; the elbow and fingers follow while both feet remain planted.

beats.label: Hold
beats.description: Inspect the silhouette and the selected surface from the front, side or an orbiting view.

beats.label: Release
beats.description: The joint chain reverses smoothly and returns to the same pose at five seconds.

studies.title: The hand, in motion.
studies.prompt: Use the shared adult female character from the licensed CC0 MakeHuman-derived GLB, with its continuous human topology, 53-bone rig, skin weights and embedded textures. Bake one fixed original identity with blonde hair, blue eyes, a softly tapered lower jaw, rounded chin, refined dentition and a neutral anatomical bodysuit; use exactly the same identity in FORM and MUSE. Keep shoulders, clavicles, waist, hips, limbs, hands and feet organically connected. Use a clean, finely textured complexion with neutral-warm facial illumination. Use the existing charcoal stage, serif interface, soft studio illumination and mint selection accent. Selected regions reuse the character surface triangles, with translucent feathered overlays and anchors that follow the evaluated skinned surface. Keep the five-second timeline, responsive controls and guided camera; manual orbit interrupts guidance. Restore the exact neutral pose at five seconds. Closely frame the same skinned character’s hand, retaining the original palm, finger webs, thumb base, nails and graduated digit proportions. Author an ordered soft closing wave through the knuckles and phalangeal joints, with the ulnar fingers starting slightly earlier and the thumb turning toward the palm. Keep the little finger rooted in the ulnar palm. Avoid intersections and abrupt joint angles. Provide selectable palm, thenar region, thumb and individual fingers, with labels attached to their moving surface.

parts.name: Thenar region
parts.description: The base of the thumb remains integrated with the palm as opposition brings the thumb toward the fingers.

parts.name: Index finger
parts.description: Three articulated phalanges bend from the knuckle, with the finger remaining connected to the palm.

parts.name: Thumb opposition
parts.description: The thumb turns at its base and bends through its own joint chain, preserving its distinct direction across the palm.

parts.name: Palm
parts.description: The continuous palm supports the finger bases and the thumb. Its skin remains connected as the hand closes.

parts.name: Middle finger
parts.description: The middle finger keeps the longest central proportion while its joints participate in the closing wave.

parts.name: Ring finger
parts.description: The ring finger closes with the neighboring fingers through its own connected joint chain.

parts.name: Little finger
parts.description: The shorter little finger emerges naturally from the ulnar palm and curls through its three joints.

Frame the same character’s ankle and complete five-toed foot. Raise the heel through the foot/forefoot joint chain while the forefoot remains supported, hold briefly, and settle.
